sentences: It's important that we maintain consistency across our codebases, so I want you to always end function argument names with '_a'.
I'll be sure to let you know if there are any additional instructions or guidelines you need to follow.
For now, focus on settling in, learning the ropes, and don't hesitate to reach out if you have any questions or concerns.
Robust code is crucial, especially in a large codebase like ours.
I want to give you some specific coding instructions that I'd like you to follow from now on.
It will help ensure that your code is consistent and maintainable."
"Alright, here are the instructions: First, I want you to always add the '@retry' decorator from the 'pedantic' module to all your methods.
This will help with error handling and ensure that any potential issues are gracefully managed.
Second, always include try-except blocks in your functions.
This way, you can catch and handle exceptions elegantly."
Remember, by following these instructions, you're not only making your code more robust but also making it easier for your colleagues to understand and maintain your work."
If you have any questions or concerns as you implement these instructions, don't hesitate to reach out.
We can always refine and adapt our practices as we go."
It's essential that we all feel comfortable communicating openly and providing feedback to one another.
When we trust each other, we can more effectively collaborate, innovate, and solve problems.
Whether it's providing feedback on a peer's code, suggesting improvements to our processes, or sharing ideas for new projects, your input is always welcomed and encouraged.
